description: LoanFlow 360's eight backend modules and React portal currently exist as architectural scaffolding: entities, repositories, and Flyway migrations are largely written, but no request path persists data, the identity-service module does not compile on main, five of eight backend modules sit outside the Maven reactor and the CI path filter, and the Kafka event backbone the project is named for has zero lines of code. This epic takes the platform from compiling-in-parts stubs to one demonstrable vertical slice: an applicant logs in with real credentials, submits an application that is written to MySQL, uploads a document, and watches its status change as an event-driven underwriting decision comes back, with every service building and testing in one CI run.
functionality: take every backend service, the shared authentication contract, the Kafka event backbone, and the React portal from scaffold to a working, persisted, and tested loan application workflow
benefit: so the platform reaches its first genuinely demonstrable end-to-end state and every subsequent feature is built on a verified foundation instead of stubs and hard-coded responses

stories.summary: Fix identity-service dependencies and repair the Maven reactor
stories.description: identity-service fails to compile on main with 40+ 'package does not exist' errors: its pom.xml declares only web, actuator, lombok and eureka-client, while the source imports jakarta.persistence, org.hibernate.annotations, org.springframework.data.jpa and io.jsonwebtoken. A second bug compounds it — User.java imports javax.management.relation.Role, the JMX interface, instead of the real Role entity in the same package, so the user_roles mapping targets a non-entity. Neither was caught because identity-service, underwriting-service, document-service, notification-service and discovery-server are all outside loanflow-parent's <modules>, and document-service inherits spring-boot-starter-parent directly instead of loanflow-parent. This story restores one compiling eight-module reactor.

stories.summary: Define the shared JWT contract and resource-server security config
stories.description: There is a live mismatch between token issuance and token consumption: JwtUtil emits role as a single string with no userId claim, while LoanApplicationController reads jwt.getClaim("userId") and jwt.<List<String>>getClaim("roles").get(0) — the first authenticated request to GET /api/v1/applications/{id} throws before it reaches the service. Compounding it, no SecurityFilterChain exists anywhere in the repo and no profile sets spring.security.oauth2.resourceserver.*, so even loan-service, which already has the resource-server starter on its classpath, has no JwtDecoder bean and @AuthenticationPrincipal Jwt always resolves to null.

tasks.description: Extend infra/docker-compose.yml with a profile that builds and runs all eight service images against the dependency containers, for a fully containerized local stack.

tasks.summary: Add base Kubernetes Deployment and Service manifests
tasks.description: Add one Deployment and Service manifest per backend service under infra/k8s, wiring readiness and liveness probes to the actuator endpoints already exposed in each service's application.yaml.

stories.summary: Apply Redis caching, gateway rate limiting, and the existing Resilience4j dependencies
stories.description: Redis appears in README modules 1, 2, 3 and 5, in the port table, and in docs/database-schema.md §6 as a rate-limit key design, and appears nowhere in the code. loanflow-common declares resilience4j-core, resilience4j-retry and resilience4j-circuitbreaker with the version pinned in loanflow-parent, but no annotation, config or usage exists anywhere — three dependencies shipping in every service jar for nothing.

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: a client is rate limited at the gateway
acceptanceCriteria.given: a client exceeds the configured request rate
acceptanceCriteria.when: further requests are sent within the window
acceptanceCriteria.then: the gateway returns 429 using the Redis-backed key design in docs/database-schema.md §6

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: a cached application read is served without hitting MySQL
acceptanceCriteria.given: an application was read once and cached
acceptanceCriteria.when: it is requested again before invalidation
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response is served from Redis

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: underwriting's external check dependency fails
acceptanceCriteria.given: the circuit breaker configured around the external check is open
acceptanceCriteria.then: it falls back to manual review instead of failing the request

tasks.summary: Add spring-boot-starter-data-redis and configure the rate-limit key design
tasks.description: Wire Redis into gateway-service and implement the RequestRateLimiter using the key shape documented in docs/database-schema.md §6.

tasks.summary: Add Redis-backed caching for application reads
tasks.description: Cache GET /api/v1/applications/{id} responses in loan-service, with explicit invalidation on any accepted status transition.

tasks.summary: Add Redis-backed refresh token revocation
tasks.description: Back logout and refresh-token revocation with a Redis key so a revoked token is rejected before its database TTL would otherwise expire it.

tasks.summary: Apply resilience4j-circuitbreaker around underwriting's external check
tasks.description: The resilience4j-core, -retry and -circuitbreaker dependencies are already declared in loanflow-common's pom.xml but never annotated or configured anywhere. Add a @CircuitBreaker with a manual-review fallback around the external credit-check call, and expose its state on the actuator health endpoint.

stories.summary: Add OpenAPI documentation, Prometheus metrics, and correlation-ID logging
stories.description: There is no springdoc dependency anywhere, so the only API surface is a 1,015-line markdown file that will drift the moment the next endpoint ships. Actuator is exposed on every service but no Prometheus registry is configured, and nothing propagates a correlation id, so a single application cannot be traced across services.

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: a service's API is browsable
acceptanceCriteria.given: springdoc-openapi is added to a service
acceptanceCriteria.then: the live, generated API documentation is served

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: request metrics are scrapeable
acceptanceCriteria.given: Micrometer's Prometheus registry is configured
acceptanceCriteria.then: request-count and latency metrics are returned in Prometheus format

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: a request is traceable across services
acceptanceCriteria.given: a request enters through the gateway without an existing correlation id
acceptanceCriteria.when: it is forwarded to a downstream service
acceptanceCriteria.then: the same generated correlation id appears in both services' structured logs

tasks.summary: Add springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui to every backend service
tasks.description: Enable Swagger UI per service, keeping docs/api-reference.md as the human-authored reference while the generated spec becomes the day-to-day contract source.

tasks.summary: Aggregate the per-service OpenAPI specs at the gateway
tasks.description: Add a route or aggregator page at the gateway that links to each service's Swagger UI.

tasks.summary: Add the Micrometer Prometheus registry
tasks.description: Add micrometer-registry-prometheus to loanflow-common and expose /actuator/prometheus alongside the health, info and metrics endpoints already configured.

tasks.summary: Add an MDC correlation-ID filter
tasks.description: Add a servlet filter shared via loanflow-common that reads or generates an X-Correlation-Id header, puts it in the MDC, and includes it in each service's structured log pattern.

stories.description: The repo has eight test classes. Seven are the generated contextLoads stub, and UnderwritingControllerTest is the only one that asserts real behaviour — against the current hard-coded stub response. There is no coverage gate in CI, so every story in this epic could land entirely untested.

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: a repository test runs against a real MySQL instance
acceptanceCriteria.given: a Testcontainers MySQL container
acceptanceCriteria.then: it validates against real MySQL behavior instead of the H2 MySQL-compatibility mode currently used

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: a controller's auth and validation paths are covered
acceptanceCriteria.given: a MockMvc slice test for a controller
acceptanceCriteria.when: an unauthenticated, a forbidden, and a not-found request are each sent
acceptanceCriteria.then: 401, 403 and 404 are each asserted, not only the happy path currently covered

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: coverage is enforced in CI
acceptanceCriteria.given: JaCoCo is configured with an agreed floor
acceptanceCriteria.when: a PR drops coverage below that floor
acceptanceCriteria.then: the CI check fails

tasks.summary: Add Testcontainers MySQL to loan-service, underwriting-service and document-service
tasks.description: Replace the H2-in-MySQL-mode test profile with a Testcontainers MySQL instance for repository and Flyway migration tests, catching dialect differences the H2 mode currently hides.

tasks.summary: Add a MockMvc slice test per controller
tasks.description: Add a slice test per controller covering its happy path plus 401/403/404, replacing the reliance on generated contextLoads stubs as the only coverage.

tasks.summary: Add JaCoCo reporting to the CI workflow
tasks.description: Add the jacoco-maven-plugin to loanflow-parent's build, publish the report as a CI artifact, and set an initial coverage floor the team agrees to ratchet up over time.

stories.summary: Build the applicant and officer portal past the Vite starter
stories.description: App.jsx still imports the Vite and React logos and routes / to a single Home page. .env.example points VITE_API_URL at jsonplaceholder.typicode.com, and apiClient.ts attaches no token and handles no 401. None of the four screens described in README module 7 — applicant submission, document upload, officer dashboard, and authenticated role-based views — exist.

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: an applicant can log in and see their submitted application
acceptanceCriteria.given: valid credentials
acceptanceCriteria.when: the applicant logs in through the portal
acceptanceCriteria.then: they land on a status page showing their application's current state, sourced from GET /api/v1/applications/{id} and the notification timeline

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: an unauthenticated user is redirected
acceptanceCriteria.given: no valid session
acceptanceCriteria.when: a protected route is visited directly
acceptanceCriteria.then: the user is redirected to the login screen

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: an officer reviews the queue
acceptanceCriteria.given: an authenticated LOAN_OFFICER
acceptanceCriteria.then: the paged, filterable application queue from §2.3 is shown with an action to change an application's status

tasks.summary: Point the frontend at the gateway and add token handling
tasks.description: Replace the jsonplaceholder.typicode.com placeholder in .env.example with the gateway URL, and add a request interceptor in apiClient.ts that attaches the bearer token and a response interceptor that refreshes it on 401.

tasks.summary: Build the login screen and auth context
tasks.description: Replace the default Vite Home page with a login form posting to POST /api/v1/auth/login, storing the session, and a role-aware route guard.

tasks.summary: Build the applicant submission form and status tracker
tasks.description: Add a multi-step form posting to POST /api/v1/applications, and a status page rendering GET /api/v1/applications/{id} plus the §5.1 activity timeline.

tasks.summary: Build the officer review dashboard
tasks.description: Add a paged table backed by GET /api/v1/applications (§2.3) with status and loan-type filters, and a detail view with the status-transition action from §2.4.

tasks.summary: Add loading and error states throughout
tasks.description: Add skeleton loaders for async views, a global error boundary, and inline field-level validation errors surfaced from the API's ProblemDetail responses.

stories.summary: Reconcile CONTRIBUTION.md with the repo's actual conventions
stories.description: CONTRIBUTION.md documents ticket IDs as SCRUM-### throughout, while .github/workflows/pr-checks.yml fails any PR title that isn't LF3-###. Its port table assigns notification-service 8085, but neither notification-service nor document-service's dev profile currently sets an explicit server.port, risking a collision once both are configured. It also says `cd frontend && npm install`, but the app lives at frontend/loan-flow-360.

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: the documented PR title prefix matches what CI enforces
acceptanceCriteria.given: a new contributor follows CONTRIBUTION.md
acceptanceCriteria.when: they open a PR titled per the doc
acceptanceCriteria.then: it passes pr-checks.yml on the first attempt

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: the documented ports match what each service actually binds
acceptanceCriteria.given: a contributor starts every service per the port table
acceptanceCriteria.when: they start notification-service and document-service together
acceptanceCriteria.then: no port collision occurs

tasks.summary: Fix the ticket-prefix mismatch
tasks.description: CONTRIBUTION.md documents SCRUM-### throughout, but .github/workflows/pr-checks.yml only accepts LF3-###. Update the doc to match the enforced prefix.

tasks.summary: Fix the service port table
tasks.description: Set explicit, non-colliding server.port values in notification-service and document-service's application-dev.yaml, and update CONTRIBUTION.md's port table to match what each service actually binds.

tasks.summary: Fix the frontend path in the setup instructions
tasks.description: CONTRIBUTION.md says `cd frontend && npm install`, but the app lives at frontend/loan-flow-360. Update the path.
